Measurements, same commands, two checkouts at the same commit:
  A. maintainer checkout /home/kara/speclang:

                      Tests  1826 passed | 58 skipped (1884)

  B. stranger checkout: git clone --depth 1 file:///home/kara/speclang /var/tmp/speclang-fresh && npm install && npm run build
     $ npm test   ->  Test Files  1 failed | 96 passed | 4 skipped (101)
                      Tests  1819 passed | 65 skipped (1884)
     failing file: tests/ci/ci005-precommit-hook.test.ts > "CI-005: pre-commit hook hardening"
     $ npx vitest run tests/ci/ci005-precommit-hook.test.ts
     Error: Hook not found: /var/tmp/speclang-fresh/.git/hooks/pre-commit

         77|     const hookDst = join(scratch, ".git", "hooks", "pre-commit");

     -> 7 tests skipped; Test Files 1 failed (1)

Nothing in the repo tells a contributor to run `git config core.hooksPath .githooks` (or copy the hook) — the missing step the suite silently requires.
Consequence for the README's own claims: README.md:90, :451 and :534 state "1826 passing | 58 skipped" with no qualifier; that number is true only in a checkout that carries the untracked hook. The same clone measures 1819 | 65.

This tick hit it in the canonical checkout: the lock `.speclang/cli-completion.json.lock` (0 bytes, mtime 2026-11-19 00:34) predated the tick by ~30 hours and every `validate` paid the full deadline.

Callers: bin/speclang:76 gates the exit hook to exactly ['validate','cascade','generate','index','guard'], so those five lanes all pay it; other commands exit before the hook.
